name: Shift logs with all three desks equal
brief:
A help line logs which desk takes each call: `A`, `B` or `C`. Count the stretches of consecutive calls in which the three desks took the same number of calls.

The whole input arrives as one string `text`:

- line 1: `n`, the number of calls;
- line 2: the `n` letters with no spaces between them.

Return the count as a string. Lines may carry extra spaces, and the text may end with blank lines.

Write `solve_equal_three(text)`.

Example. For `"5\nABCAB\n"` the stretches `ABC`, `BCA` and `CAB` each hold one call per desk. No other stretch is balanced, so the answer is `"3"`.
constraints: $O(n)$ time is the target. Counting the calls in every stretch is too slow.
All tests share a 5-second time limit. Answers can pass $10^{9}$.
hint: Keep running counts `a`, `b` and `c`. A stretch is balanced exactly when the pair `(a - b, b - c)` is the same before it and at its end, so count how often each pair has been seen.

examples.note: Each of the three stretches of length 3 holds one A, one B and one C.
Four stretches of length 3 are balanced, and so is the whole log, which makes 5.

tests.call: solve_equal_three("200000\n" + "".join("ABC"[(i * i + i // 7) % 3] for i in range(200000)) + "\n")

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. The large tests need the step from counting every stretch to a dict keyed on the two differences of the running counts.
notes: Two differences of the running counts fix the balance, so equal pairs bound a balanced stretch.
One difference is not enough: `CCC` keeps `a - b` at 0 but is not balanced.
One pass with a dict of pairs, so the work is $O(n)$.

planted.slip: It keys only on `a - b`, so a stretch of calls to desk C alone looks balanced.
It never records the empty start, so balanced stretches that begin with the first call are lost.
It counts the calls of every stretch, which is $O(n^2)$ and too slow for 200,000 calls.
